suppliers.interface: Let L be a smooth local four-form Lagrangian for fields phi on an oriented four-manifold and let a chosen variational decomposition be delta L=E(phi) dot delta phi+d theta(phi;delta phi). For commuting smooth variations define omega(phi;delta1 phi,delta2 phi)=delta2 theta(phi;delta1 phi)-delta1 theta(phi;delta2 phi). For a compact oriented three-surface Sigma put Omega_Sigma=integral_Sigma omega.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $A,B:H\to H$ be non-negative operators. For such an operator $A$, set $\operatorname{supp}(A):=(\ker A)^\perp$, where $\ker A$ is the kernel of a linear map ([[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]); this extends the density-operator support convention in [[def-qc-density-operator]]. If $\operatorname{supp}(A)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(B)$, define

$$D(A\|B):=\operatorname{tr}(A\ln A)-\operatorname{tr}(A\ln B).$$

Here $\ln A$ is defined spectrally on the positive eigenspaces of $A$ with $0\ln0:=0$, and $\ln B$ in the cross term is restricted to $\operatorname{supp}(B)$; the support condition ensures that $A$ vanishes on $\ker B$, so the omitted kernel contributes zero. If $\operatorname{supp}(A)\nsubseteq\operatorname{supp}(B)$, set $D(A\|B):=+\infty$. In particular, $D(0\|B)=0$. For density operators this is the finite-dimensional **quantum relative entropy**. The logarithms are natural, so the value is in nats; the base-two value is $D_2(A\|B):=D(A\|B)/\ln2$.

suppliers.interface: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited through the stated supplier chain. Let M act on H with normalized cyclic separating Omega. Let S be the closure of S0(x Omega)=x* Omega, and write S=J Delta^(1/2). Define sigma_t(x)=Delta^(it) x Delta^(-it), t dimensionless. Delta is positive injective, with possibly unbounded inverse; its imaginary powers are bounded unitaries.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit and $\delta\in R$. For each $n\ge0$, let $F_n:=R\langle u_1,\ldots,u_{n-1}\rangle$ be the free associative unital $R$-algebra on the indicated symbols ([[lem-hh-free-associative-ring-and-relations-descent]]). When $n=0$ or $n=1$, the symbol set is empty and $F_n=R$.

Let $I_n$ be the two-sided ideal generated by

$$u_i^2-\delta u_i\quad(1\le i<n),\qquad u_i u_j-u_j u_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$

and

$$u_i u_{i+1}u_i-u_i,\qquad u_{i+1}u_i u_{i+1}-u_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le n-2).$$

The abstract **rank-$n$ Temperley–Lieb algebra** is the presented $R$-algebra

$$P_n(R,\delta):=F_n/I_n.$$

Thus its defining relations are $u_i^2=\delta u_i$, $u_i u_{i\pm1}u_i=u_i$, and $u_i u_j=u_j u_i$ for $|i-j|>1$. The definition of a presented $R$-algebra and its universal property are those of [[lem-hh-free-associative-ring-and-relations-descent]].

suppliers.interface:
Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], and let
$\nabla$ be its unique torsion-free $g$-compatible connection supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Fix a nonempty
connected open set $O\subseteq M$. A **selected stationary thermal carrier** on
$O$ consists of a smooth future timelike vector field $\xi$ and a smooth
positive scalar field $T:O\to(0,\infty)$, where $T$ is measured in kelvins,
such that $\xi$ is a Killing field of $g$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-killing-field]]. Equivalently, the criterion is
$\nabla_{(a}\xi_{b)}=0$ by
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]]. The round brackets mean
symmetrization with factor $1/2$. The choice of $\xi$ specifies the thermal congruence; no
coordinate chart or universal observer field is selected.

Set $N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and $u:=\xi/N_\xi$. Then
$g(u,u)=-1$. In the length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$, $u$ is
dimensionless and $cu$ is the physical four-velocity, with $c>0$ in
$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. For a fixed Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in
$\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, define the inverse-temperature vector
$\beta:=u/(k_BT)$, with units $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and the Killing-normalized
temperature field $T_K:=N_\xi T$. Thus $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$; this definition
does not assert that $T_K$ is constant.

For a smooth chemical-potential scalar $\mu:O\to\mathbb R$ in joules, put
$\zeta:=\mu/(k_BT)$, a dimensionless scalar. Define the rest-space metric,
derivative, acceleration, expansion and shear by
$$h_{ab}:=g_{ab}+u_au_b,\qquad D:=u^a\nabla_a,\qquad a_b:=u^a\nabla_au_b,\qquad \theta:=\nabla_au^a,\qquad \sigma_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)}-\frac13\theta h_{ab}.$$
Here $a$, $\theta$ and $\sigma$ have inverse-length units; the physical
proper acceleration is $c^2a$. The smooth tangent-bundle structure used by
the cited GR suppliers assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice
[[def-countable-choice]]; no stronger choice principle is part of this
definition.

Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative ring with unit, $\delta\in R$, and suppose $[2],\ldots,[n]$ are units. The projector $p_n$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-recursion-over-unit-denominators]] has coefficient $1$ on the identity diagram, is nonzero and idempotent, and is annihilated on both sides by each $U_i$ for $1\le i<n$. Its corner is $p_n\mathrm{TL}_n p_n=R p_n$, so it is the unique idempotent with identity coefficient $1$ and those two-sided annihilation conditions. For $n\ge1$,

$$\operatorname{ptr}_n(p_n)=\frac{[n+1]}{[n]}p_{n-1},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_n(p_n)=[n+1].$$

Only the displayed denominator units are assumed; $\delta$ need not be a unit.

suppliers.interface:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as defined by [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $G,c,\hbar,\eta,M_0,M_{\min}>0$ be the relevant constants and initial/cutoff data of [[prop-tgr-ideal-evaporation-accounting]], with $0<\eta\leq1$ and $0<M_{\min}<M_0$. Let
$$
M(t_\infty)=(M_0^3-3\alpha t_\infty)^{1/3}, \qquad \alpha=\frac{\eta\hbar c^4}{15360\pi G^2}, \qquad \tau=\frac{M_0^3-M_{\min}^3}{3\alpha}
$$
be the positive solution and cutoff supplied by that proposition.
Use the diagnostic of [[def-tgr-emitter-quasistatic-diagnostic]]. Then
$$
\epsilon_{\mathrm{qs}}(t_\infty)=\frac{2G\alpha}{c^3M(t_\infty)^2} \leq\frac{2G\alpha}{c^3M_{\min}^2}.
$$
For any $\epsilon_0>0$, the condition $M_{\min}^2\geq2G\alpha/(c^3\epsilon_0)$ therefore implies $\epsilon_{\mathrm{qs}}(t_\infty)\leq\epsilon_0$ throughout $[0,\tau]$.

There is also an exact finite-interval bound. If $0\leq t_\infty\leq t_\infty+\Delta t\leq\tau$ and
$$
\delta:=\frac{3\alpha\Delta t}{M(t_\infty)^3}\leq\frac12,
$$
then
$$
\frac{M(t_\infty+\Delta t)}{M(t_\infty)}=(1-\delta)^{1/3}, \qquad \left|\frac{M(t_\infty+\Delta t)}{M(t_\infty)}-1\right| \leq\frac{2^{2/3}}{3}\,\delta.
$$
Both bounds are exact internal consequences of the adopted ODE. They give no error bound between that ODE and an unconstructed Einstein–quantum backreaction solution.

Assume Countable Choice. Let
$$\mathcal H=L^2((0,\infty),dk;\mathbb C),\qquad \langle h,q\rangle_2=\int_0^\infty\overline{h(k)}q(k)\,dk,$$
using the second-variable-linear convention. For
$f\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ define
$$h_f(k)=\sqrt{\frac{k}{4\pi}}\int_{\mathbb R}f(U)e^{ikU}\,dU\quad(k>0).$$
Then $h_f,h_{\bar f}\in\mathcal H$, and $f\mapsto h_f$ is continuous on each fixed-compact-support test space. With the bosonic Fock conventions of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]], define on its finite-particle domain
$$J(f)=a(h_{\bar f})+a^\dagger(h_f).$$
This is a complex-linear operator-valued distribution on that invariant domain. For real $f$, its closure is $\overline{J(f)}=\sqrt2\,\Phi(h_f)$, where $\Phi(h_f)$ is the closed Segal field of [[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]]; the corresponding Weyl one-parameter group has generator $i\Phi(h_f)$. The vacuum two-point form is positive type and has boundary kernel
$$C(s)=-\frac{1}{4\pi(s-i0)^2},$$
where $s-i0$ means the distributional limit from $s-i\epsilon$, $\epsilon\downarrow0$.

For $\kappa>0$ with units of inverse length, let $u,U$ have units of length and set
$$U_\kappa(u)=-\kappa^{-1}e^{-\kappa u},\qquad u_\kappa(U)=-\kappa^{-1}\log(-\kappa U)\quad(U<0).$$
For $g\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ put $f_g(U)=g(u_\kappa(U))$ for $U<0$ and $f_g(U)=0$ for $U\ge0$, and define $j_\kappa(g)=J(f_g)$. The zero extension is smooth and compactly supported. Its vacuum covariance is the positive-type distribution
$$C_\kappa(s)=-\frac{\kappa^2}{16\pi}\,\operatorname{csch}^2\!\left(\frac{\kappa}{2}(s-i0)\right).$$
Here the notation is fixed as follows: for $b=\kappa/2$, set $Y_b(s)=\sinh(bs)/b$. Since $Y_b'(s)=\cosh(bs)>0$ and $Y_b(s)\to\pm\infty$ as $s\to\pm\infty$, it is a smooth increasing diffeomorphism. Define $\operatorname{csch}^2(b(s-i0)):=b^{-2}Y_b^*((y-i0)^{-2})$, where
$$\langle Y_b^*T,\varphi\rangle:=\left\langle T,\varphi(Y_b^{-1}(y))(Y_b^{-1})'(y)\right\rangle.$$
This is a one-dimensional chiral test-coordinate model. It asserts no restriction of a four-dimensional field to a null curve.

Use the Lorentzian geometry, units, charge sign, potential $A$, field $F=dA$,
compensator $\Lambda_\xi$, and $C^2$ charged trajectory $x(s_m)$ of
[[def-tgr-charged-liouville-data]]. Assume the global potential symmetry
$\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$. Define
$$H_\xi:=-g(P,\xi)+q\Phi_\xi=-g(P,\xi)-cq\Psi_\xi.$$
Then $\iota_\xi F=-d\Psi_\xi$, and $H_\xi$ is constant along every interval
on which the trajectory obeys the stated Lorentz equation. It is invariant under
$A\mapsto A+d\chi$, $\Lambda_\xi\mapsto\Lambda_\xi+\xi(\chi)$. Replacing the
potential reference by $\Phi_\xi+C_0$ changes $H_\xi$ by $qC_0$.

This is a conditional mathematical statement about curves satisfying the
displayed equation. It asserts neither existence of such curves for arbitrary
initial data nor that the model describes nature.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $A,b>0$, put $\beta=\pi/b$ and $L=A/b^2$, and define the analytic kernel
$$C(z)=-A\operatorname{csch}^2(bz),\qquad \operatorname{csch}w=1/\sinh w.$$
Use the angular-frequency convention
$$\widehat\varphi(\omega)=\int_{\mathbb R}\varphi(s)e^{-i\omega s}\,ds,\qquad \varphi(s)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}\widehat\varphi(\omega)e^{i\omega s}\,d\omega$$
for Schwartz functions $\varphi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$, where Schwartz space has seminorms $\sup_s|s^m\varphi^{(n)}(s)|$ and a tempered distribution is a continuous complex-linear functional on that space. Define its Fourier transform by the bilinear pairing $\langle\widehat T,\varphi\rangle=\langle T,\widehat\varphi\rangle$; test functions are not conjugated.

For $0<\epsilon<\beta$, $C_\epsilon(s)=C(s-i\epsilon)$ is a smooth $L^1$ function. These regularizations have a limit $C_{A,b}\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R)$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$, denoted $-A\operatorname{csch}^2(b(s-i0))$. The kernel is holomorphic on $-\beta<\operatorname{Im}z<0$, has period $i\beta$, and its tested boundary values obey
$$C(s-i\beta+i0)=C(-s-i0).$$
The Fourier transform of $C_{A,b}$ is the continuous nonnegative function
$$S_{A,b}(\omega)=\frac{2\pi(A/b^2)\omega}{e^{\pi\omega/b}-1},\qquad S_{A,b}(0)=\frac{2\pi L}{\beta}=\frac{2A}{b}.$$
In particular $S_{A,b}(-\omega)=e^{\beta\omega}S_{A,b}(\omega)$ for $\omega>0$. The zero-frequency value is the removable limit, and the boundary and Fourier assertions are distributional, not pointwise integrals at a double pole.

If the coordinate has a specified unit, $s,z,\beta,\epsilon$ have that unit and $b,\omega$ its reciprocal. If $A$ has covariance units, $L$ has those units times the square of the coordinate unit and $S_{A,b}$ has those units times the coordinate unit.

In particular, for $\kappa>0$ in inverse length, take $A=\kappa^2/(16\pi)$ and $b=\kappa/2$. Then $L=1/(4\pi)$, $\beta=2\pi/\kappa$, and $C_{A,b}$ is precisely the tested chiral covariance $C_\kappa$ of [[lem-tgr-exponential-current]]. Its spectrum and detailed balance are
$$S_\kappa(\omega)=\frac{\omega}{2(e^{2\pi\omega/\kappa}-1)},\qquad S_\kappa(0)=\frac{\kappa}{4\pi},\qquad S_\kappa(-\omega)=e^{2\pi\omega/\kappa}S_\kappa(\omega)\quad(\omega>0).$$
Here $C_\kappa$ has units of inverse length squared and $S_\kappa$ inverse length. This is a two-point strip and detailed-balance statement, including the specified chiral current as a specialization. It does not assert a norm-continuous $C^*$-algebra KMS dynamics or an exact detector transition probability.

Let $O$ be a connected open set in a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold, let $u$ be a smooth future unit timelike vector field on $O$
($g(u,u)=-1$), and let $T:O\to(0,\infty)$ be smooth. Define
$\beta:=u/(k_BT)$, $h_{ab}:=g_{ab}+u_au_b$,
$D:=u^a\nabla_a$, $a_b:=u^a\nabla_au_b$,
$\theta:=\nabla_au^a$ and
$\sigma_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)}-\theta h_{ab}/3$ as in
[[def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers]]. Then $\beta$ is a Killing field of
$g$ (equivalently $\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}=0$ by
[[def-gr-killing-field]] and
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]]) if and only if
$$DT=0,\qquad \theta=0,\qquad \sigma_{ab}=0,\qquad h_a{}^b\nabla_b\log T=-a_a.$$
No hypersurface-orthogonality or vanishing-vorticity condition is assumed.

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as defined in [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the mathematical context for the tested-current, Fourier and temporally smeared field constructions used below.

Use the length-coordinate, unit, and reference conventions of [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. Adopt two distinct model branches.

**Reduced exponential-current branch.** Choose a constant $\kappa>0$ in inverse metres and a smooth Killing field $\xi$ on a declared domain in the TGR framework. The real parameter $u$, measured in metres, is the selected flow parameter for $\xi$; the reference event and normalization of this flow are fixed as part of the model. Set the exponential coordinate $U_\kappa(u)=-\kappa^{-1}e^{-\kappa u}$. Adopt the positive-chiral-current vacuum and tested current $j_\kappa$ constructed in [[lem-tgr-exponential-current]]. Its mathematical two-point covariance is the tested boundary $C_\kappa$ there; use its angular-frequency spectrum $S_\kappa$ and detailed-balance convention exactly as stated in [[lem-tgr-thermal-contour-spectrum]]. The exponential ray map and the choice of $\kappa$ are model inputs. If $\xi$ and $\kappa$ are identified with a generator and geometric surface gravity of a particular horizon, that identification is an additional physical assumption; no collapse geometry, four-dimensional horizon restriction, scattering factor, or backreaction is derived here.

**Massless acceleration branch.** Adopt the massless scalar and Minkowski vacuum of [[post-qft-free-field-model]]. Use the actually defined temporal smearing along the smooth proper-time hyperbola and its tested covariance from [[lem-tgr-timelike-scalar-acceleration]]. The curve-smeared field is not a sharp-point field. Its accelerated spectrum and finite-switch coefficient are used only with the conditional hypotheses recorded in that lemma and in [[lem-tgr-spectral-thermometer]].

For either branch, select an energy gap $E>0$ joules and define a two-state, continuous-time rate model with ground state $g$, excited state $e$, and model-time parameter $t\ge0$ measured in seconds. In the reduced branch, no identification of $t$ with proper time along a spacetime curve is assumed. In the acceleration branch, take $t=\tau\ge0$ along the proper-time hyperbola supplied by [[lem-tgr-timelike-scalar-acceleration]]. In the reduced branch let $\gamma_{\rm red}>0$ have units metres per second and set $r_\uparrow=\gamma_{\rm red}S_\kappa(E/(\hbar c))$ and $r_\downarrow=\gamma_{\rm red}S_\kappa(-E/(\hbar c))$. In the acceleration branch let $\gamma_{\rm acc}>0$ have units square metres per square second and set $r_\uparrow=\gamma_{\rm acc}S_a(E/\hbar)$ and $r_\downarrow=\gamma_{\rm acc}S_a(-E/\hbar)$. Here $c>0$ is metres per second, $\hbar>0$ is joule-seconds, and the frequency arguments have units inverse metres and inverse seconds, respectively. These choices make both rates inverse seconds. The adopted population $p(t)$ of state $e$ is the solution of $p'(t)=r_\uparrow(1-p(t))-r_\downarrow p(t)$ with supplied $p(0)\in[0,1]$. This differential equation is the entire effective two-state model; the rates are adopted inputs, not exact QFT transition probabilities.

Only when a selected construction also supplies a density state and a normalized finite measurement instrument may an outcome be read using [[post-qft-constructed-model-and-measurement]]. No such state, instrument, detector apparatus, or observed outcome is supplied here. The postulate asserts no general thermalization, exact all-order transition probability, KMS state, or experimental temperature reading.

Use the time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, Levi-Civita connection, smooth future unit observer congruence, and length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$ of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. Here a **frame** means this smooth observer field $u$ with $g(u,u)=-1$ and its pointwise rest spaces; it does not mean a coordinate chart or a tetrad. On a nonempty open region $O$, take a $C^2$ fixed-composition state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$ with $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, state function $e\in C^2(X)$, and $T=\partial_{\sigma_p}e>0$ as adopted by [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]]. The mathematical state maps are $n=v^{-1}$, $s=n\sigma_p$, $\varepsilon=ne$, and $p=-\partial_v e$; their meanings and units are those in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[def-tgr-framework-units]].

Write $u_b=g_{bc}u^c$ and define the rest-space projector, derivative along the observer congruence, expansion, acceleration, and spatial symmetric trace-free shear by
$$\Delta^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b,\qquad \Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^a u^b,\qquad D=u^a\nabla_a,\qquad \theta=\nabla_a u^a,\qquad a_b=u^c\nabla_c u_b,$$
$$\sigma_{ab}=\Delta_a{}^c\Delta_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)}-\frac{\theta}{3}\Delta_{ab},$$
where parentheses denote the averaged symmetric part. Put $Y_b=\nabla_bT+Ta_b$ and $Z_b=\nabla_b(\mu/T)$, using the chemical potential $\mu$ from [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. The number current, stress tensor and entropy current in the selected branch are
$$J^a=nu^a+V^a,\qquad \mathsf T^{ab}=\varepsilon u^a u^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab}+u^aQ^b+Q^au^b+\pi^{ab},\qquad S^a=su^a+\frac{Q^a}{T}-\frac{\mu V^a}{T},$$
with $u_aV^a=u_aQ^a=u_a\pi^{ab}=0$ and $\pi^{ab}$ symmetric and trace-free. Adopt the source-free balances $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ and $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}=0$ together with the first-order gradient closures
$$\Pi=-\zeta c\theta,\qquad \pi^{ab}=-2\eta c\sigma^{ab},\qquad Q^a=-\frac{\kappa}{c}\Delta^{ab}Y_b,\qquad V^a=-L\Delta^{ab}Z_b.$$

Here $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; $\theta$, $a_b$ and $\sigma_{ab}$ have inverse-length components; $\Pi$, $\pi^{ab}$ and $Q^a$ have units Pa; $\zeta,\eta\in C^1(O)$ have units Pa s; $\kappa\in C^1(O)$ has units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$; and $L\in C^1(O)$ has formal units $\mathrm{marker^2\,K\,J^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$. The temperature and chemical-potential gradients have units K m$^{-1}$ and J marker$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ m$^{-1}$, respectively. The coefficient fields satisfy $\zeta,\eta,\kappa,L\geq0$. On $O$, require $\Pi$, $\pi^{ab}$, $Q^a$, and $V^a$, together with the resulting $J^a$, $\mathsf T^{ab}$, and $S^a$, to be $C^1$. The state map and state function are $C^2$ and $u$ is smooth, as specified above. These regularities make the displayed balances and entropy-current divergence pointwise classical expressions; require the balances to hold pointwise.

Each application declares a nonempty open regime of the pointwise state values and first covariant derivatives of $u,T,\mu/T$ (with the listed algebraic constraints) on which the constitutive model is used. The regime separately requires $J$ to be future timelike. Since $u_aV^a=0$, this condition is $n>0$ and $g_{ab}V^aV^b<n^2$, as follows from $g(J,J)=-n^2+g(V,V)$ and $-u_aJ^a=n$. It is an additional applicability restriction, not a consequence of the gradient closures.

This is an adopted constitutive model for one declared material regime. The closures are not derived from geometry, measurements, or the second law; they do not assert that a solution exists, that the model applies to every material, or that the branch is causal, stable, or globally entropy-increasing. No empirical observation is supplied.

For a selected fixed-composition, single-material branch, adopt a local-equilibrium description on an open state domain $D\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ with a supplied function $e\in C^2(D,\mathbb R)$ and $T:=\partial_{\sigma_p}e>0$. Here $v$ is the rest volume per selected material marker, $\sigma_p$ is entropy per marker, and $e$ is energy per marker, including the rest-energy contribution; their types and SI units are those in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. Here “comoving” means that local state values are referred to the observer-congruence rest spaces of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]; no orthogonal rest-slice foliation or finite-region volume integral is presupposed. For an admissible local continuum parcel, let $N_p>0$ be its real marker amount, $V>0$ its supplied proper-volume parameter, and $S\in\mathbb R$ its supplied total entropy, with $(V/N_p,S/N_p)\in D$. The quantities $V/N_p$ and $S/N_p$ have the per-marker state meanings and units of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. This model assigns energy $E=N_p e(V/N_p,S/N_p)$. Treating the real marker amount as a particle count is part of the fixed-composition continuum model, not a claim about discrete microscopic transitions or a consequence of the mathematical marker definition.

This is an adopted constitutive/local-equilibrium premise for the stated material and regime. It does not derive $e$ microscopically, assert a measured equation of state, impose a spacetime conservation equation, imply a universal gas law, or make the local parcel energy additive with the energy of an arbitrary self-gravitating region. Rest energy belongs in $e$; if a rest mass $m$ is specified, its contribution is $mc^2$, not $m$ in SI units. No entropy-maximization, quantum Gibbs representation, or global gravitating thermodynamic limit is assumed.
If E=0 and both variations obey delta_i E=0, then d omega=0. For a compact region with oriented boundary Sigma2-Sigma1+B, Omega_Sigma2-Omega_Sigma1=-integral_B omega.

Use the physical Kerr–Newman family parameterized by the connected strict subextremal domain
$$\mathcal P:=\{(m,a,q)\in\mathbb R^3:m>0,\ m^2>a^2+q^2\},$$
with its current SI parameter map and selected horizon conventions from [[pthm-tgr-kn-family-mechanics]]. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as defined in [[def-countable-choice]], the mathematical premise used by the current Kerr–Newman and reduced spectral supplier proofs. Let $S_H:\mathcal P\to\mathbb R$ be the $C^1$ entropy state function adopted in [[post-tgr-thermodynamic-horizon-identification]], measured in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. Assume that postulate's reversible-heat identity $\delta Q_{\rm rev}=dE_{\rm par}-\Omega_{\rm SI}dJ_{\rm SI}-\Phi_{\rm SI}dQ_e=T_KdS_H$ on $\mathcal P$. Also assume its pointwise temperature identification: for each $x=(m,a,q)\in\mathcal P$, the reduced branch parameter is held fixed at $\kappa=\kappa_{\rm geom}(x)=s(x)/D(x)>0$, and the smooth reference-temperature field is $T_K:\mathcal P\to(0,\infty)$ with $T_K(x)=T_{\rm red}(x)=\hbar c\kappa_{\rm geom}(x)/(2\pi k_B)$. Then there is a constant $s_*\in\mathbb R$, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, such that throughout $\mathcal P$
$$S_H=\frac{k_B}{4\ell_P^2}A_H+s_*=\frac{k_Bc^3}{4G_N\hbar}A_H+s_*,\qquad \ell_P^2:=\frac{G_N\hbar}{c^3}.$$
The deduction determines the area coefficient within this adopted model and leaves the entropy zero unselected. It does not identify $S_H$ with a statistical microstate count or an outside-state entropy.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold
of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], and let $U\subseteq M$ be open. For any
complete explicitly supplied named smooth classical matter-model instance
$\mathcal M=(\mathcal C_m,\mathcal E_m,\mathsf J_m,\mathsf T_m)$ of
[[post-tgr-smooth-horizon-energy-condition]], retain its specified matter-field
bundles, configuration fields, exact equations and constraints, constitutive
inputs, regularity, and additional domain or data hypotheses. Take a smooth
admitted configuration $\Psi\in\mathcal C_m[g,F]$ satisfying
$\mathcal E_m[g,F;\Psi]=0$ on $U$, and use the same source maps
$j=\mathsf J_m[g,F;\Psi]$ and $T^m=\mathsf T_m[g,F;\Psi]$. Assume the
equation-based Einstein–Maxwell equations and restricted total-stress null
energy condition of that postulate for this model and configuration. The
claim is uniform over these supplied named models, without requiring a
matter action or choosing a particular matter closure. Let $H\subset U$ be a
smooth embedded null hypersurface with a smooth nowhere-zero future null
generator field $k$ satisfying $\nabla_k k=0$. In the definitions of
[[def-tgr-horizon-screen-family]], $k$ is affine and its screen expansion is
$\theta=\operatorname{tr}_{\bar g}B$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as defined in [[def-countable-choice]]. Let
